verified.exploit_entry_point: file.Store.Push with a caller-supplied AnnotationTitle: without unpacking (resolveWritePath -> pushFile -> os.Create) and with AnnotationUnpack=true (pushDir -> extractTarGzip -> extractTarDirectory). All security cases run through Push; digest and descriptor are computed in the test with the go-digest module, never with product code.
sites: content/file/utils.go:264-275 (ensureLinkPath validates a joined, cleaned path but returns the literal target that the kernel resolves)
content/file/utils.go:231-259 (resolveRelToBase compares strings and Lstats only the parent components of the cleaned path)
content/file/utils.go:159-215 (extractTarDirectory writes members with no resolved-containment check)
content/file/utils.go:278-292 (writeFile opens the final path with O_CREATE|O_TRUNC and follows a terminal link)
content/file/utils.go:184-192 (hard-link member is applied with os.Link using the raw archive Linkname)
content/file/file.go:609-628 (resolveWritePath performs only a lexical filepath.Rel containment check)
content/file/file.go:472-483, 486-512 (pushFile os.Create and pushDir ensureDir follow a link component under the working directory)
routes: C1/T1: unpack a layer whose relative link targets lexically stay inside the layer but are resolved by the kernel through a previously extracted link; a same-named regular member then writes through it outside the working directory
C1/T2: unpack a regular member whose final path component is already a link out of the layer; writeFile opens it with O_TRUNC and writes outside
C2/T4: push a member whose name traverses a link directory under the working directory; the lexical check passes and os.Create/MkdirAll follow the link outside

C3/T3: unpack a hard-link member whose relative linkname names a file in the process working directory; os.Link aliases it into the store and a later same-named regular member writes through the alias, changing a file outside the store
verified.project_tests_run: At the pinned commit the environment image builds with `go build ./...` and runs the project's own `go test ./content/file` (all pass). The reference fix keeps that package green; every check patch was exercised against the package locally as well.

traps.shape: a relative link target whose lexically cleaned form stays in the layer while one component in the literal target is itself a previously extracted link, so the path that was validated is not the path the kernel resolves; a regular member with the same name then writes through it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: ensureLinkPath already validates every link target against the layer dir, and a target whose lexical clean is the layer dir itself is indistinguishable from '.', so the target reads as contained and the check as complete.
traps.realistic_because: the reported route: an ordinary untrusted layer passed to the public Store.Push entry point with unpacking enabled

traps.shape: the 'no link between base and target' walk starts at filepath.Dir(path) and stops at '.', so a link that sits at a member's final component is never inspected before the regular member is opened and written through
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the 'no symbolic link allowed between base and target' loop reads as a check on the whole destination, but it starts at filepath.Dir(path) and stops at '.', so the final component of a member is never inspected before the file is opened.

traps.shape: a hard-link member's relative Linkname is checked as if resolved against the link's directory, but os.Link is handed the raw literal, so the process working directory decides which file is linked; a later same-named regular member writes through the alias outside the store
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the inline comment states that ORAS does not generate hard links and calls the behaviour a known limitation that will not be addressed, so hard-link members look out of scope for a pull-hardening fix.

traps.shape: a member name whose path crosses a directory link under the working directory passes the lexical Rel check; os.Create for a plain member and MkdirAll for the unpacked layer directory both follow it and write outside the root
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report and the extraction guards are about tar members; resolveWritePath already rejects '..' names, and a plain file push (or the layer dir created by pushDir) is a different API that never had a symlink check.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the push path's containment check is lexical only

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

A.summary: the push path's lexical write-path check is not resolved against symlinks

B.summary: the unpack path follows a chain of links that the check validated lexically, and writes regular members through a terminal link
